description: This chart displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each representing the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—across different difficulty levels for a “Zero-Shot” task. Each pie chart is divided into four colored segments corresponding to these categories, with a shared legend indicating that teal represents N+K+, yellow represents N−K+, orange represents N−K−, and red represents N+K−. The “easy” chart shows the largest segment (teal, N+K+) at 55.4%, followed by yellow (N−K+) at 38.3%, a small orange slice (N−K−) at 4.6%, and a tiny red slice (N+K−) at 1.7%. The “medium” chart has the teal segment (N+K+) at 58.8%, yellow (N−K+) at 35.4%, orange (N−K−) at 4.8%, and red (N+K−) at 1.8%. The “hard” chart shows the yellow segment (N−K+) at 37.3%, orange (N−K−) at 37.9%, teal (N+K+) at 18.1%, and red (N+K−) at 6.7%. All percentage values are explicitly labeled within their respective slices, and the segments appear to be arranged in descending order of size within each pie chart.
